title: Kenya Safari Packing List: What to Bring, Wear and Leave at Home
meta_title: Kenya Safari Packing List: 16 Essentials for a Light Bag
meta_description: Kenya safari packing list: what to wear, flight luggage limits, colours to avoid, the plastics ban and a printable checklist from our Nairobi team.
excerpt: Our Kenya safari packing list covers what to wear, 15 kg light aircraft limits, colours to avoid, seasonal extras and what to leave at home.
content:
A good Kenya safari packing list is short: neutral, layered clothing for cold dawns and hot afternoons, a soft bag that fits light aircraft limits, binoculars, a camera, sun and insect protection, your medicines and documents. Most travellers need less than they think, because many safari camps offer laundry and game drives are relaxed affairs.

The hard part is knowing what matters in Kenya specifically: luggage weight rules on bush flights, the plastics ban in parks, tsetse-fly colours, chilly Mara mornings and dusty roads. This Kenya safari packing list guide gives you a printable checklist, what to wear and why, what changes by season and region, and what to leave at home, written by our safari team in Nairobi.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Quick Facts

  • Bag type: Soft duffel or holdall; hard suitcases are refused on many light aircraft
  • Weight limit (flights): Airkenya allows 15 kg per person including hand luggage (checked October 2026)
  • Best colours: Khaki, olive, tan and beige; avoid dark blue and black in tsetse areas
  • Mornings: Cool in the Mara, Nairobi and Laikipia, so pack a fleece
  • Plastics: Plastic bags banned since 2017; single-use plastics banned in parks since June 2020
  • Power: Kenya uses UK-style Type G three-pin plugs at 240V
  • Cash: Bring small US dollar or Kenya shilling notes for tips and extras

What Should Be on a Kenya Safari Packing List?

A Kenya safari packing list needs four groups of items: practical clothing in neutral colours, health and sun protection, optics and electronics, and documents and money. For a typical 5 to 10 day trip, one soft bag of about 15 kg is enough if you plan to use camp laundry halfway through.

The Kenya safari packing list table below is the core checklist we suggest to travellers on road and fly-in safaris. Adjust the numbers for the length of your trip, and remember that you will rewear trousers and fleeces far more than you would at home, since you spend most of the day sitting in a vehicle.

How Much Luggage Can You Take on a Kenya Safari?

On a road safari in a Land Cruiser or safari van, you can usually bring one medium soft bag plus a daypack per person. On a fly-in safari, light aircraft set strict weight and shape limits, and that is the rule that shapes your whole Kenya safari packing list.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Light aircraft limits on a fly-in safari

Airkenya, one of the main scheduled carriers to the Masai Mara, Amboseli, Samburu and Laikipia, allows 15 kg per person on all its services, and that total includes hand luggage (checked October 2026). Bags must be soft-sided. Its guideline size for a checked bag is 60 x 45 x 33 cm, and handbags, small backpacks and camera bags count towards the 15 kg.

Excess baggage is carried only if there is space, at US$5 per kg, and Airkenya sells 5 kg or 10 kg bundles up to 48 hours before departure (checked October 2026). Other airlines and charter flights set their own rules, so confirm the allowance on your ticket before you finalise your Kenya safari packing list. If you are combining a fly-in safari with a beach stay, most Nairobi hotels and airline offices can store a second bag while you are in the bush.

Road safaris and mixed itineraries

Road safaris are more forgiving, but space in the vehicle is shared, so build your Kenya safari packing list around a soft duffel of 60 to 70 litres. Hard-shell suitcases are awkward on rough roads and in tent storage. Keep a small daypack with you in the vehicle for your camera, binoculars, water, sunscreen, a fleece and any medicines you need during the day.

If you are flying on to Tanzania, the same rules usually apply, and our Tanzania safari packing checklist covers the Serengeti and Ngorongoro side, including cooler crater rim nights.

What to Wear on a Kenya Safari: Colours, Layers and Shoes

The clothing side of a Kenya safari packing list is simple: wear loose, breathable clothes in khaki, olive, tan, beige or soft green, in layers you can shed as the day warms up. Neutral colours hide dust and attract fewer biting insects than very bright or very dark clothes.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Why are some colours a bad idea on safari?

Tsetse flies, found in parts of some Kenyan parks such as Tsavo and Shimba Hills, are drawn to dark blue and black, which is why tsetse traps are made from that cloth. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention advises neutral, medium-weight clothing with long sleeves in tsetse areas, because the flies bite through thin fabric and repellent does not reliably stop them.

White and pale cream clothes turn brown within a day on dusty roads, and neon colours can make animals wary on walking safaris. Many travellers also skip camouflage prints, which are associated with the military in much of East Africa. Plain, earthy colours simply work best.

Layering for cold mornings and hot afternoons

Much of safari Kenya sits high up: Nairobi is around 1,700 metres and the Masai Mara and Laikipia plateaus are mostly above 1,500 metres. Game drives start around sunrise in an open-roof vehicle, so the first hour can feel cold, especially from June to August. By late morning it is usually warm, and in Samburu, Tsavo and on the coast it is hot all day.

The answer on any Kenya safari packing list is a T-shirt, a long-sleeved shirt and a fleece, plus a light waterproof jacket in the rainy months. A buff or scarf protects your face from wind and dust, and a beanie is worth its small weight if you are going to the Mara or Laikipia between June and September.

Shoes for game drives, walks and camps

Footwear on a Kenya safari packing list can be simple. Light walking shoes or trail trainers are enough for game drives, nature walks and camp paths, and sandals are handy for evenings. You only need proper hiking boots if you add a guided walking safari over rough ground or a Mount Kenya or Kilimanjaro climb, which needs its own gear list.

How Does Your Kenya Safari Packing List Change by Season and Region?

Your Kenya safari packing list changes mainly with rain and altitude. In the long rains (roughly April to May) and short rains (roughly November) add a proper rain jacket and quick-dry clothes. In the cool dry months add warmer layers for the highlands, and for the hot north and coast pack the lightest fabrics you own.

Which Cameras, Binoculars and Electronics Should You Bring?

For the gear on your Kenya safari packing list, bring binoculars for each person, a zoom camera, two spare batteries, memory cards and a power bank. Charging in tented camps is often limited to set hours or the main area, so spare power matters more than a second camera body.

Photo by Ran Berkovich on Unsplash

Camera and lens

A zoom lens reaching 300mm or more is ideal for wildlife, and a modern phone is fine for landscapes and camp shots. A bean bag or a small cloth bag you fill with rice in Nairobi steadies a long lens on the vehicle window. Pack a soft lens cloth and a blower brush, because dust is constant on Kenyan roads.

Plugs, charging and connectivity

Kenya uses the UK-style Type G three-pin plug at 240V, so add an adapter to your Kenya safari packing list if you live outside the UK. Many safari vehicles have USB or inverter charging, and most camps have Wi-Fi in the main area at least. A head torch is essential, as camp paths are dark at night and you will often be escorted to your tent.

If photography is the main reason for your trip, our wildlife photography safaris use vehicles with more space for camera gear and longer time at sightings.

Health, Documents and Money for a Kenya Safari

The paperwork on a Kenya safari packing list matters most: pack your passport, printed eTA approval, travel insurance details and any vaccination certificate in a waterproof pouch, with prescription medicines in original packaging, a first-aid kit and some cash in small notes.

Health items for your Kenya safari packing list

Your Kenya safari packing list should include insect repellent (DEET or picaridin), any antimalarials your doctor prescribes, rehydration sachets, plasters, blister pads, painkillers, antihistamines and hand sanitiser. Our guide to Kenya safari vaccinations and malaria advice explains what to discuss with your travel clinic before you go.

Documents and cash

No Kenya safari packing list is complete without travel approval: every visitor needs an approved electronic travel authorisation before flying, and our Kenya eTA guide walks through the application. For money, bring a bank card plus some newer, undamaged US dollar notes or Kenya shillings in small denominations, and read our guide to tipping in Kenya so you know how much to set aside for guides and camp staff.

Insider Tips

  • Pack in cubes: Fabric packing cubes keep a soft bag organised and replace banned plastic bags
  • Wear your heaviest items: Fly in with your boots and fleece on to save weight on light aircraft
  • Use camp laundry: Many camps offer laundry, so pack for 4-5 days, not your whole trip; some ask guests to wash their own underwear
  • Keep a daypack handy: Camera, binoculars, water, sunscreen and a fleece should stay with you in the vehicle
  • Bring a dry bag: A small dry bag protects electronics from dust and sudden showers
  • Small notes only: Large notes are hard to change in the bush

What Should You Not Pack for Kenya?

Leave plastic carrier bags, single-use plastic bottles and cutlery, hard-shell suitcases, expensive jewellery, camouflage clothing and anything you would hate to see covered in dust. Kenya's plastics rules are enforced, and the other items simply cause problems on light aircraft and dirt roads.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Kenya banned plastic carrier bags in 2017, and the UN Environment Programme reports that single-use plastics are banned in Kenyan parks and beaches from 5 June 2020, including water bottles, cups, plates, cutlery and straws. Pack toiletries in fabric wash bags and refill a reusable bottle from the filtered water most camps provide.

Also leave off your Kenya safari packing list a heavy hairdryer (many camps cannot power one), more than one pair of smart shoes, and drones, which need permits from Kenyan authorities and are restricted in parks. If you are visiting a Maasai village, modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees is respectful, and our fly-in safari packages team can tell you exactly what fits the planes you will use.

Frequently Asked Questions

What should be on a Kenya safari packing list?

A Kenya safari packing list should cover neutral layered clothing (three or four shirts, two trousers, a fleece, a rain jacket), closed shoes, a hat, sunglasses, sunscreen, repellent, binoculars, a camera with spare batteries and a power bank, a first-aid kit, your medicines, passport, eTA and small cash notes.

How much luggage can I take on a safari flight in Kenya?

Light aircraft flights in Kenya have strict limits. Airkenya allows 15 kg per person in soft-sided bags, and that 15 kg includes your hand luggage (checked October 2026). Its guideline bag size is 60 x 45 x 33 cm, and extra kilos can sometimes be bought in advance. Other carriers set their own limits, so check your ticket before you pack.

What colours should I not wear on a Kenya safari?

On a Kenya safari, avoid dark blue and black in areas with tsetse flies, and skip bright colours such as white or neon on game drives, as they show dust and stand out. Khaki, olive, tan, beige and soft greens are the safest choices. Many travellers also avoid camouflage prints, which are associated with the military in much of East Africa.

Can I bring plastic bags to Kenya?

No. Kenya banned plastic carrier bags in 2017, and since 5 June 2020 single-use plastics such as water bottles, cups, plates, cutlery and straws are banned in national parks, beaches, forests and conservation areas. Pack a reusable water bottle and use zip-up fabric pouches or packing cubes instead of plastic bags in your Kenya safari luggage.

Do I need warm clothes for a safari in Kenya?

Yes, a fleece or light down jacket belongs on every Kenya safari packing list. The Masai Mara, Nairobi and Laikipia sit at high altitude, so early morning game drives in an open vehicle can feel cold, especially from June to August. Days usually warm up quickly, which is why light layers you can take off work better than one heavy coat.

Final Thoughts

The best Kenya safari packing list is light, neutral and layered: one soft bag within the flight limit, warm layers for dawn, sun and insect protection, binoculars, spare batteries, your documents and some small notes. Everything else is optional.
